{"number":402,"title":"Claudinite growth: extract lessons from 2026-08-07 conversation logs","body":"Final hindsight pass over the 17 conversation logs past the 10-day retention window (all captured 2026-08-07), plus a fresh pass over the 2026-08-16/17 logs. Six new lessons landed in `edfringe/RULES.md`:

- amend the latest commit (not `git filter-branch`) once the `task-lifecycle` Stop hook has already fired
- never `curl` `api.github.com` directly for a run's status — it returns a look-alike JSON error with no `status` field, so a naive poll loop spins silently forever; poll through the GitHub MCP tools
- `pull_request_read method=get_status` is a dead signal on this repo — use `get_check_runs`
- a deleted workflow file's old runs can't be purged by any session tool (no `actions:write` DELETE endpoint in the MCP toolset) — hand it to the owner
- `npm i -D playwright` in the repo root is the same footgun as the scratchpad variant, just quieter
- `index.html`'s Leaflet map loads from `unpkg.com`, which the sandbox proxy blocks — stub it before driving the page

None of the six clear the check-the-world test (all are session/API runtime behavior, not static repo signatures), so all land as prose. The activity half (commit 65de9fd, PRs #397/#399, issues #401/#237) turned up nothing durable — all fleet/engine plumbing.

One candidate was considered and deliberately **not** landed: a session hitting the auto-mode classifier's block on `git commit` touching `.github/workflows/` and recovering via the GitHub API tools instead. This repo's own rules ("A capture pass must never land a rule that teaches routing around a safety or permission denial") bar that shape of lesson regardless of framing, so it's being reported to the owner instead — see the tracking issue.

Refs #400

{"number":269,"title":"Claudinite growth: extract lessons","body":"Daily `grow_with_claudinite/growth-extract` run (dispatch #268).

**Activity half: skipped.** The dispatch's Context named no commits, merged PRs or issues, so there was no window to work over.

**Conversation half:** fresh pass over the 19 logs captured 2026-08-05…08-07 on `conversation-logs`. Two keepers, both landing as prose in `.claudinite/local/packs/edfringe/RULES.md`:

| Lesson | Where | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Playwright: `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium` is a **symlink** onto the pinned chrome binary, not a directory as the rule claimed — and `npm i playwright` into the scratchpad is a trap, since a fresh install pulls a newer Playwright than the image and then demands a browser build (`chromium_headless_shell-1234` vs the vendored `-1194`) the sandbox cannot download | existing "Verifying UI changes visually" section | sessions on #251, #258, #264 all took the detour on 2026-08-07; the symlink and the working import were re-probed in this run |
| Watching a workflow/scheduler run: use `mcp__github__actions_get` / `actions_list`, never a shell `curl` poll of `api.github.com` — `gh` isn't installed, shell egress to the API is per-environment and has been denied mid-session, and a denied `CONNECT` returns a proxy body rather than JSON so an `until`-loop neither terminates nor explains itself | new section | #249 burned two round-trips before the MCP call answered in 5s; #251 backgrounded an `until curl …; sleep 15` loop, abandoned it and fell back to a blind `sleep 90` for a run `actions_get` reported already complete |

**Deduped out**, all already documented in the local packs or at their call site: the `task-lifecycle` and `comment-classification` Stop-hook blocks (both have their own RULES.md sections); the refresh-worker `git push` root cause (a long comment at the usage site in both `worker.sh` files); the ad-hoc-workflow egress bypass and the `*.edfringenow.com` allowance (already landed, `382706d` / `3fc07c0`); the data-file caching TTLs and the ticket-availability wire shape (product requirements, not work-procedure rules — the pack's own rule says so).

**Upgrade pass (prose-to-checks) over this run's own additions:** neither converts. Both constrain sandbox tooling behaviour rather than a static signature anywhere in this tree, so there is nothing a check could observe.

**Retention prune:** not run — Context did not state it was due. No log was deleted.

`bash scripts/verify.sh` green (206 tests, 33 JS parse-checked, 4 Python byte-compiled, normalizer self-test OK).

Refs #268

{"number":278,"title":"Claudinite growth: extract lessons","body":"Growth-extract run for slot `d2026-08-08` (tracking #277). Two lessons landed in this repo's own local packs; nothing else changed.

**Activity half** — over the 14 named commits and the merged PRs in the window:

- `edfringe-data/RULES.md` — **"The API stamps performances in UTC — cross the zone once, at the edge."** From #275 / PR #274: `dateTime` is a real UTC instant, and slicing its digits shifted all 60,115 performances an hour. Records the single crossing point (`normalize.local_date_start`), that no stage downstream re-converts, that "now" is read in Edinburgh via `js/clock.js` rather than the device, and that a conversion change is a full-snapshot change whose day-file boundary shifts are expected rather than data loss.
- `edfringe/RULES.md` — **"Retiring a practice: delete it, state the rule that replaces it, don't narrate the change."** From the owner's review on PR #240, which removed both the retired-probe narration added to three docs *and* the newly built `edfringe-workflows-allowlisted` check. Carves out that measured evidence justifying a rule stays; what goes is narration of a superseded way of working.

**Conversation half** — fresh pass over the 2026-08-06/07 captures. Their friction (the `task-lifecycle` and `comment-classification` Stop blocks, blind sleeps, auto-merge arming) is already covered by existing rules, so nothing new landed from them beyond the PR #240 review lesson above.

**Retention prune** — `retention_days: 10`. Six logs stamped before 2026-07-29T04:02Z got their final hindsight pass (nothing above the bar) and were removed from `conversation-logs` in a separate `[skip ci]` commit on that branch. It is not merged anywhere and its history is untouched.

**Upgrade pass** — neither addition constrains a static, observable signature a check could assert confidently, so both stay prose.

`scripts/verify.sh` and both local pack test suites are green.

{"number":420,"title":"Claudinite growth: extract lessons","body":"Conversation half — final hindsight pass over the 12 logs stamped 2026-08-09 (past `retention_days: 10`), plus a fresh pass over the 15 logs from 2026-08-10 through 2026-08-14 that no prior run's summary had explicitly cited as covered. Activity half skipped per this run's dispatch Context (no substantive default-branch change in the window).

Ten lessons landed:

- `edfringe/RULES.md`: Leaflet's unpkg.com block can be worked around with a real curl'd copy, not just a no-op stub (#318); get the browser's own Network/Cache-Storage evidence before guessing a repro for a live-data bug report (#309); three refinements to the polling section — a curl-based Monitor false-positive, overlapping background sleeps, and a subagent's placeholder "completed" text (#349, #332); `subscribe_pr_activity` gets denied here when used mid-session, poll directly instead (#335, #341); a dispatched subagent's work is void if you don't actually wait for it (#296); `pull_request_read get_files` overflows on a large PR (#303); don't resolve the "name a neighbour, not its specifics" rule by pointing at a `.claudinite` path — it trips `claudinite-isolation` (#341); wiki-growth competitor research is WebSearch, not WebFetch (#300).
- `edfringe-data/RULES.md`: two independently-cached wire files joined by key need a fingerprint, or a backend generation change silently breaks the join at ~6% instead of 100% (#309).
- `edfringe-requirements/RULES.md`: reproduce a golden-flake with the harness's own pixel comparator, not a raw byte/hash compare (#335).

Upgrade pass (prose-to-checks): none convert — all ten are runtime/tool/process behavior with no static signature a check could observe, or (the `.claudinite`-path trap) already enforced by the existing `claudinite-isolation` check.

One candidate lesson from #351 was reviewed and rejected: a proposal to land a rule telling future sessions to retry a classifier-blocked git push once before escalating to `needs-human`. That is the same shape of standing route-around-a-permission-denial instruction already reverted once in this repo (issue #359, PR #361) — this repo's own rule bars it regardless of framing, so it was not landed; flagged for the owner in the tracker instead.

`bash scripts/verify.sh` green — 273 tests, 171 JS parse-checked, 4 Python byte-compiled, normalizer self-test OK; 0 blocking, 4 advisory (all pre-existing).

Closes #419

{"number":694,"title":"Claudinite growth: rule revalidation","body":"Weekly `claudinite-growth/rule-revalidation` pass over this repo's local pack (scope: `.claudinite-settings.json`'s `claudinite-growth.pack_paths`, unset here, so the default `.claudinite/local/packs` → `.claudinite/local/packs/edfringe-now/`).

Re-probed every claim in `RULES.md` (and its `references.md`) whose truth lives outside this repo — the Claude harness's own tool contracts, GitHub/MCP tool behaviour, and this session's egress policy — and corrected what no longer held. Read-only probes only; nothing was merged, deleted, or notified as part of probing.

## Corrected (stale → fixed in this diff)

1. **Egress "Observed so far"** (`## Reaching the network`) — the 2026-09-04 "general egress open" observation is no longer current. Probed 2026-09-13 with `curl` against 8 hosts plus `$HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status`: `fringeplan.com`, `maze.co`, `www.lyssna.com`, `unpkg.com`, `example.com`, `edfringe-tikketr-web-api.equhost.com` all got `CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`, confirmed as **policy** denials (not origin) via the proxy's own `recentRelayFailures` log; only `www.edfringe.com` (200) and `fonts.googleapis.com` (404, i.e. tunnel succeeded) got through. Added as a third data point — the policy visibly swings both ways within days, which is exactly why the rule's own directive ("probe it in this session first") stands unchanged.
2. **`edfringe-tikketr-web-api.equhost.com` reachability** (data-pipeline section) — same probe reproduced a CONNECT-level policy denial today, reverting from the 2026-09-04 "server-side 403" (tunnel succeeded, origin refused) back to the 2026-08 "denied at CONNECT" shape. Added as a third dated data point.
3. **`actions_list`/`list_workflow_runs` per_page claim** — old text: "lowering `per_page` does not fix it" (evidenced by identical overflow at 25/10/3/2/1). Retested live: `list_workflow_runs` with no `perPage` overflowed at ~59K chars; with `perPage: 3` and again `perPage: 1` it returned cleanly, no truncation. The MCP tool's handling of `perPage` has evidently been fixed since that finding — corrected the rule to "pass `perPage` explicitly" rather than "don't bother lowering it."
4. **`list_pull_requests` merged-field claim** — old text: "`merged_at` is never populated, `fields` or not." Retested against three real closed-and-merged PRs (#682, #676, #670), with and without a `fields` filter: `merged` still always decodes `false`, but `merged_at` **is** populated in every case (cross-checked against `pull_request_read get` on PR #385, `merged: true`, as ground truth). Corrected the rule to use `merged_at` as the landed-ness signal instead of grepping `origin/main`'s commit subjects.
5. **`pull_request_read method=get_files` overflow claim** — old text: "treat it as skip the diff, not something to retry." Retested PR #207 (46 files, the PR named in the original claim): `perPage: 100` still hard-overflows exactly as before, but `perPage: 10` returned successfully (large, but under the limit). Corrected from "don't retry" to "retry at a smaller `perPage`."
6. **`download_workflow_run_artifact` tool-shape claim** — `ToolSearch` with `select:mcp__github__download_workflow_run_artifact` returns "No matching deferred tools found"; a keyword search shows it is now a `method` value on `mcp__github__actions_get` (`resource_id` = artifact ID), not a standalone tool. Corrected the invocation shape in the rule; the substance (the returned URL is an off-allowlist blob-storage host the proxy denies at CONNECT) is unchanged and not itself re-probed today.

## Holds (reconfirmed, no change)

- **`gh` CLI is not installed** — `which gh` → exit 1, no output.
- **The harness blocks a bare `sleep N`** — read directly off the current Bash tool's own contract text ("Long leading `sleep` commands are blocked... use Monitor with an until-loop"), the most authoritative and current source available.
- **Playwright/Chromium pre-install, `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, the `chromium` symlink, and the `index.mjs` import with no `executablePath`** — `echo`'d the env var, `ls`/`readlink`'d the symlink chain, and ran a live `node -e` importing `/opt/node22/lib/node_modules/playwright/index.mjs` and launching Chromium (`chromium.launch()` succeeded, version 141.0.7390.37).
- **`search_issues`/`list_pull_requests`/`pull_request_read` shrink with `fields`/`minimal_output`** — consistent with this run's own `fields`-narrowed `list_pull_requests` calls, each a small payload.

{"number":613,"title":"Merge the three local packs into edfringe-now","body":"Closes #612

Part of the fleet-wide consolidation in missingbulb/Claudinite#1691 — one local pack per repo, named for the repo.

`edfringe`, `edfringe-data` and `edfringe-requirements` become `edfringe-now`, under a heading per surface: working in the repo, the data pipeline, the requirements harness. All seven checks and both tasks move under the one manifest unchanged.

The split bought no routing anyone used. All three were declared by hand, none was fingerprinted, and a session loaded all three together on every turn — so the only thing three manifests separated was which file a rule was typed into.

## What moved, and what followed it

Two file collisions resolved: `edfringe-data/README.md` becomes `DATA.md` beside the rules it explains, and its `pack.test.mjs` becomes `data-checks.test.mjs`.

Three references followed the rename rather than being left dangling — a grep sweep after the move, not before:

- **`package.json` and `scripts/verify.sh`** both spell `.claudinite/local/packs/edfringe/tasks/` explicitly in their `node --test` globs. Left alone, both tasks' tests would have silently stopped running while everything still went green. (The pack's own `test-globs-in-step` check exists to catch these two drifting apart — it does not catch them drifting *together*.)
- **The caching rule** cross-referenced `edfringe-data/RULES.md`, which is now a section of the same file.

One path is deliberately **not** updated: the `claudinite-isolation` rule quotes a comment a past sweep wrote (`"see the declarations under .claudinite/local/packs/edfringe/tasks/"`). That is a record of a specific past edit, so it stays verbatim.

The local `VERSIONS.md` files do not come across — a local pack is neither versioned nor distributed, and its commits are the record.

## Folders touched

```
.claudinite/local/packs/   three packs become edfringe-now; 7 checks, 2 tasks, tests moved
.claudinite/               claudinite-rules.GENERATED.md regenerated
.claudinite-settings.json  three declarations become one
scripts/, package.json     the node --test globs follow the tasks directory rename
```

## Verification

- `npm test` — **274 pass, 0 fail**.
- `node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — **exit 0, 0 blocking**.

The checks earned their keep on the way: three `config` findings for the stale declarations, one `rules-index-current` for the unimported new pack, and a `rules-line-length` advisory. One assertion inside `pack.test.mjs` needed its expected string repointed after the rename — the check was right, the expectation was stale.

Three `file-placement` advisories remain in `plan/lib/`. They are pre-existing on `main` and this diff touches none of that code.

## Noted, not fixed here

The merged `RULES.md` is ~940 lines and 34 rules, roughly three times the next-largest local pack in the fleet. Merging all three was the explicit call and I have not second-guessed it, but a file that long is scanned by heading rather than read — and the three headings this PR introduces are the seams a later split would follow. Recorded on #612 rather than treated as free.

Fixes #249, whose two gaps this split resolves at the root:

  * refresh_ticket_status.py wrote only data/days/*.json, which the planner
    has never loaded — every hourly commit changed nothing it could see. It
    now writes statuses through the master and regenerates every derived
    file from it, so one source of truth feeds all of them.
  * It stopped at today, leaving every future date frozen at the last manual
    full scrape. It now covers today through the end of the run; one listing
    pass already returned those performances, so the wider window is free.

Two invariants hold the caching up, both silent if broken, both now tested:
the venues.json lookup lists are append-only (extend_lookup), since a
four-day-old catalogue is decoded against a venues.json fetched today; and
shows.min.json carries nothing day-varying, asserted per wire performance.

Also fixes the hydrate round-trip test, red on main: it expected the
master's `description` back from the catalogue, which deliberately leaves it
to descriptions.min.json. It now strips the field and asserts it survives in
that sidecar instead, so "moved" can't become "lost".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Hold the now page's day file for an hour, not a day

The page answers "what can I get into right now" and draws SOLD OUT stamps
that refresh-tickets rewrites hourly, so a day-long reuse was a cache that
outlived its own data: a visitor returning after lunch would have seen the
morning's availability. An hour matches the refresh that feeds it.

The reuse worth having survives — the url is keyed by date, so this only
ever concerned same-day revisits, and a reload or a reopened tab still skips
the download.

{"number":544,"title":"refresh-tickets crashes on an out-of-range performance stamp; turn the scraping tasks off","body":"Owner's words: "Fix the bug in #379. Also turn off all the scraping tasks (either on github actions or claudinite tasks)".

**The bug.** `refresh-tickets`' prework exits 1 with

```
File "scraper/normalize.py", line 269, in local_date_start
    local = parsed.astimezone(FESTIVAL_TZ)
OverflowError: date value out of range
```

`local_date_start` guards only against a *malformed* stamp (`ValueError` from `fromisoformat`). A well-formed but extreme stamp — `0001-01-01T00:00:00.000Z` reproduces it — parses fine and then overflows in `astimezone`, because Europe/London's LMT offset pushes it below `datetime.min`. The whole pass dies on one junk performance rather than skipping it, which is what the function's documented contract already promises for a value it cannot file.

**Turning the scraping off.** The two scheduled Claudinite tasks (`edfringe/refresh-shows`, `edfringe/refresh-tickets`) are what run on their own; the two GitHub Actions scraping workflows (`scrape.yml`, `prices.yml`) are `workflow_dispatch`-only and never fire unattended.

## 2026-07-26 · born · Phase 3: cut over to the Claudinite per-repo task scheduler (#101)
- **Reason:** replaced "Refresh today's ticket status (hourly)" and its sixteen hand-spelled August
  cron lines.
- **Actor:** @missingbulb (owner).
- **Model:** Claude
- **Mechanism:** an hourly scheduler task in the `edfringe` pack, `agent_model: 'none'`, whose
  precondition acts only in August, 08:00-23:59 Edinburgh.
- **Landed:** #101, Refs missingbulb/Claudinite#394

## 2026-08-06 · policy-changed · push to origin HEAD:main explicitly (#235)
- **Reason:** diagnosed as `actions/checkout` leaving the branch with no upstream, failing the bare
  push and filing a needs-human issue (#231).
- **Actor:** @missingbulb (owner).
- **Model:** Claude
- **Mechanism:** `worker.sh`.
- **Landed:** #235

## 2026-08-06 · policy-changed · return the checkout to main instead of forcing a refspec (#236)
- **Reason:** the run logs disproved #235's diagnosis: the real cause was an earlier task in the
  same scheduler run leaving the checkout on its own branch, and `HEAD:main` would have pushed that
  unreviewed commit straight to main.
- **Actor:** @missingbulb (owner).
- **Model:** Claude
- **Mechanism:** `worker.sh` returns to main before the scraper writes anything, then pushes bare.
- **Rejected:** the explicit `HEAD:main` refspec of #235.
- **Landed:** #236

## 2026-08-07 · policy-changed · the worker writes through the master, today to the end of the run (#252)
- **Source:** #249: the catalogue could only earn a long cache TTL by giving up the ticket status
  that changed in it hourly, so status moved to its own sidecar.
- **Reason:** it wrote only the day files, which the planner never loads, and stopped at today,
  leaving every later date frozen at the last full scrape.
- **Actor:** @missingbulb (owner).
- **Model:** Claude Opus 5
- **Mechanism:** `worker.sh` writes statuses through the master and regenerates every derived file.
- **Landed:** #252, Fixes #249

## 2026-08-12 · policy-changed · once a day instead of hourly (#340)
- **Reason:** hourly through August put up to sixteen commits a day into main and expired every
  browser's day file as often, for a status that is a snapshot however often it is taken.
- **Actor:** @missingbulb (owner).
- **Model:** Claude Opus 5
- **Mechanism:** cadence `daily+1h`, after refresh-shows' `daily` anchor; the 08:00-23:59 hours
  window dropped, since it would have gated the one daily evaluation out, and the August gate kept.
- **Landed:** #340

- **Reason:** the canon's task-declaration check retired `daily+1h`; the offset existed only to
  order this task after refresh-shows on a shared checkout.
- **Actor:** the Claudinite update run.
- **Mechanism:** `frequency: daily` with `schedule_after: edfringe/refresh-shows`.
- **Landed:** #472, Refs #471

- **Source:** the owner's request on #544 to turn off all the scraping tasks.
- **Actor:** @missingbulb (owner).
- **Model:** Claude
- **Mechanism:** `frequency: 'manual'`, the contract's off switch; the declaration test pins it so

- **Landed:** #545, Closes #544

# Committing

- **One concern per commit.** If two changes could each stand alone, split them; a message that
  wants numbered items is the split talking. (concern-commit)
- **Reference the issue, when the change has one** — `Refs #n`, or `Fixes #n` / `Closes #n` where
  the commit finishes it. A change tracked by its PR alone references nothing.
  (reference-issue-change)
- **A landed commit is revised by a new commit**, never a rewrite of that one.
  (landed-commit-revised)
- **Stage by name** — `git add <paths>` for the files this commit is about; `-a` sweeps in whatever
  else was in progress. (stage-name)

Closes #869

Backfills the provenance of the local pack `edfringe-now` from its history, using the `backfilling-provenance` method. This comes before cleaning up its RULES.md. No rule, check or task changes.

## Counts
- **35 owed files filled**: 34 were empty, including `_pack.md`, and 1 (`report-capability-unavailable.md`) held only the conversion's entry. `apply --backfill` replaced that placeholder `born` (dated 2026-09-20) with the real birth in #609. It carried over the placeholder's Reason and Retire-when.
- **`_declined.md` created**, with 4 candidates:
  - #85: the "ad-hoc PR has no linked issue" friction. It is canon workflow, not local.
  - #124: the scraper's stdout-buffering fix. The fix belongs at its call site.
  - #402: recovering from a classifier-blocked workflow commit through the API tools.
  - #420: "retry a classifier-blocked push once". This one and the #402 candidate are both route-around-a-denial lessons, which this repo bars.
- `check edfringe-now` now shows no empty or conversion-only file, exit 0.

## Where the brief's derivation was corrected
- **Elements that came from `edfringe-requirements` and `edfringe-data`**: the brief could not trace them back past #613, because it read only the `edfringe` paths. I traced them by hand:
  - The harness rules were born in #316.
  - `red-ci-lanes` was born in #353.
  - `reproducing-golden-flake` was born in #420.
  - `lookup-lists-append` and `shows-min-json` were born in #252.
  - `now-compared-against` and `conversion-change-full` were born in #278.
  - #613 is now recorded as a `moved` on every element that existed then.
- **`logic-rule` and `behavior-rule`**: the brief matched the one-word triggers "logic" and "behavior" to #85 and #353. Both were really born in #316.
- **`checking-deployed-site` and `reading-403-proxy`**: born in #262. #609 reworded them.
- **MCP call-shape rules**: born in #391 (#420 for `get_files`). The #694 revalidation reworded them.
- **Tasks**: born in #101. Policy changes are recorded through #235, #236, #252, #340, #472, #545, #586, #601, #670 and #731.

## Minimal entries (the evidence ran out)
These got a `born` that gives only the carrier and the #316 source, plus their `moved` entry:
- `logic-rule`
- `geolocation-exists-only`
- `css-freeze-does`
- `fonts-arrive-google`
- `vendoring-web-fonts`
- `floating-popup-dies`
- `ready-networkidle`

`now-compared-against` shares only the #278 incident as its Reason. #670's policy changes to both tasks carry no Reason, because the update PR stated none.

## pack.mjs and DATA.md
- `pack.mjs`: 1961 to 1522 bytes. The 2026-09-04 consolidation paragraph moved to the `_pack` `merged` entry.
- `DATA.md`: 1694 to 1191 bytes. What moved to `_pack` entries: the edfringe-data "split out because..." paragraph, the "Distilled from" list and the old enforcement table. It now lists the three data checks as they stand in `edfringe-now`. The stale `pack.test.mjs` name is corrected to `data-checks.test.mjs`.

## Checks
- `provenance.mjs check edfringe-now`: exit 0, nothing owed.
- `check_the_world.mjs`: 0 blocking. 2 advisories, both already on main (`claude-md-length`, `product-wiki-freshness`).
- `check_the_work.mjs`: 0 blocking. 1 advisory, `provenance-change-recorded` on `report-capability-unavailable.md`. This is the expected case: the backfill replaced what the conversion wrote.
- `npm run verify`: all checks passed.

```
.claudinite/local/packs/edfringe-now/provenance/  35 files filled, _declined.md created
.claudinite/local/packs/edfringe-now/             pack.mjs header and DATA.md trimmed of history
```

entries.description: Get information on a specific pull request in GitHub repository.

after.description: Cursor for pagination, used only by the get_review_comments method. Pass the endCursor from the previous page's PageInfo to fetch the next page.

method.description:
Action to specify what pull request data needs to be retrieved from GitHub. 
Possible options: 
 1. get - Get details of a specific pull request.
 2. get_diff - Get the diff of a pull request.
 3. get_status - Get combined commit status of a head commit in a pull request.
 4. get_files - Get the list of files changed in a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 5. get_commits - Get the list of commits on a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 6. get_review_comments - Get review threads on a pull request. Each thread contains logically grouped review comments made on the same code location during pull request reviews. Returns thread metadata and comments with nullable current and original line-range coordinates (line, start_line, original_line, original_start_line). Current coordinates are omitted when unavailable, such as for outdated comments. Use cursor-based pagination (perPage, after) to control results.
 7. get_reviews - Get the reviews on a pull request. When asked for review comments, use get_review_comments method. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 8. get_comments - Get comments on a pull request. Use this if user doesn't specifically want review comments. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 9. get_check_runs - Get check runs for the head commit of a pull request. Check runs are the individual CI/CD jobs and checks that run on the PR.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

Use when adopting Claudinite on a repo that already carries a CLAUDE.md, when a person wants their machine-local instructions carried properly, or when asked to convert instruction prose into a pack.
- fetching-from-the-web: Reading a page or a file from the web in a session — exact bytes over a summarizing fetch, and what a 403 or an egress block means. Use before any WebFetch or curl, and when a fetch is denied.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- git-github-advanced: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the baseline lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- improve-comments: Improve a repo's own comments as a pass of their own: delete, correct, add the why. Use when working a repo's comments deliberately (the basics pack's improve-comments task), never as a side effect of another change.
- learning-a-technology: Teach a repo a new technology for a job of its own. Use when asked to make a repo do something with a technology nobody there has used yet (host it on X, send through Y, publish to Z), or to "research how to do this correctly" and "create a skill" for it.
- merge-to-main: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner approves the current branch or PR, or asks to merge or land it into main.
- production-retrospective: Design and file the review that comes back on its own once a larger element has lived in production. Use when designing a larger element, when filing a migration plan's chain, when a merge completes a design-doc'd element, or when defining a new retrospective class for a pack, a repo, or the fleet.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- releasing-a-cloudflare-site: How a site served from Cloudflare is released — the version contract, the guards that stop a release loop or a half-release, forcing one, rolling one back, and which parts of Cloudflare only a person can change. Use when changing the release task, the wrangler config or the analytics loader, and when a release parks.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- revalidating-rules: Re-probe the pack rules whose truth lives outside the repository — harness tool contracts, token reach, whether an MCP tool exists, a platform's behaviour — and correct the ones that have gone stale. Use when a revalidation sweep runs over a corpus of packs, or when asked whether a rule's environmental claim still holds.
- searching-for-a-tool: Finding a harness tool by name — the select form for a deferred tool, and what an empty search means. Use before any ToolSearch, and when a search finds nothing.
- triaging-usage-findings: Turn a usage-review finding that has lasted into a proposed change - read the element's provenance first, settle which of the rule's causes it is, and write the edit itself rather than a description of it. Use when a usage-triage run hands you lasting findings, or when an owner asks what to do about one.
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- working-with-generated-files: Working with a file a test or tool generates — naming it, changing the generator rather than the file, and resolving its merge conflicts by regenerating. Loaded for any edit of a GENERATED file.
- write-a-requirement-leaf: How a requirement leaf is written in the executable spec — the backtick-numbered one-liner with its detail collapsed under it, and which kind (surface snapshot, behavior, logic, saga, per-project, e2e singleton) its case takes. Use when adding or reshaping a requirement line in requirements.md.
- write-a-saga: How a saga case is written — a multi-step story captured as a golden storyboard or one animated APNG golden — steps, captions, frame budget, the real entry point, delay stripping and gesture marking. Use when authoring or changing a case under the saga kind.
- writing-handover-issues: How to write a task list a PERSON will execute — a handover issue, an adoption checklist, a "steps only a human can do" list. Use when filing or editing any issue whose body asks a human to click, set, register or copy something. Not for issues describing work you will do yourself.
- writing-migration-plans: How a plan's phases are ordered so nothing stalls mid-run. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan (including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file), when asked to run a plan as a chain of ad-hoc tasks, and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-pack-prose: How pack prose is written - RULES.md rules, SKILL.md bodies and check text in a Claudinite pack, local or canon - brevity, structure, triggerability, findability, the marker that names a rule's provenance file. Loaded for any edit of a pack's RULES.md or SKILL.md, and when landing a lesson as prose.
- writing-repo-scanning-checks: How a check that scans the repo picks its file set, strips comments before matching a forbidden token, and proves itself silent against real sources. Loaded for any edit of a coded or declared check.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.json or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- writing-wiki-pages: How a product-wiki page is written and grown — the Key insights header, citation, what a source actually supports (attribution, independent voices, public proxies), correction without deletion, the growth log, sample-data, when a pass writes nothing. Loaded for any edit under product-wiki/.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- anthropic-skills:docs: docs (living docs people share, comment on and edit; use only when the user asks for one: names a doc, document, page, memo, spec, PRD, runbook or write-up, asks for somewhere to share or keep editing something, or says yes to your doc offer; a plan, comparison, summary or notes asked in chat stays in chat (at most a one-line doc offer); a report, status update, recap or "something I can send them" with no form named → ask first: reply, doc or file?; tabs hold tables and live charts too; a pasted claude.ai/code/artifact/… link may be a doc: check with docs tools first; not HTML pages, apps or plain chat answers; a .docx/.pptx/.xlsx/PDF asked for by name → that format's skill): asked for one → no docs-connector instructions in context? call the docs connector's `guide` with topic.instructions first, then create the doc (headings only, no body) before any search, file read or plan, even with files attached. Documenting code means docstrings or repo docs, not a doc.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead, even if they will email or print it. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
